definition: A reference type is a type whose variable holds a reference to a value stored elsewhere, not the value's own bytes. Two variables can refer to the same object, so a change through one is visible through the other. Objects and arrays are reference types in many languages.
details: Assigning a reference copies the reference, not the object. A later mutation is shared; a later reassignment of one variable is not.
examples: Two variables pointing at the same list
Passing an object into a function that mutates it
